property_summary: For any caller that is not the current owner, setOwner must revert and leave the owner unchanged; the buggy version allows a non-owner to change the owner.
After any successful setOwner call by the current owner, the owner should be the address passed to the function; the buggy version sets it to zero instead.
The reference contract only allows the original owner to change the owner, so when called by a non-owner the owner stays the same, but the buggy version allows anyone to change it.
The reference ensures owner remains unchanged when a non-owner calls setOwner, but the buggy version allows any caller to change it.
For any caller, a successful call to setOwner returns true; the bug violates this by allowing non-owners to succeed, thereby changing owner when the reference would have reverted.

After any call to setOwner, the owner is either the original owner (if the call reverted) or the newly provided address only if the caller was the original owner; the bug version violates this by allowing any caller to change owner to any address.
The owner can only be set by the current owner (owner can change), but the buggy tx.origin check allows any caller that is initiated by the original owner to change the owner.

After any sequence of calls to setOwner, the owner variable always equals the last address that successfully passed the access check; the buggy version allows an arbitrary caller to become owner when executed via a contract called by the original owner, violating the invariant that only the current owner can change the owner through a direct EOA call.
After any call to setOwner, the owner variable must equal the _owner argument passed, but the buggy version sets it to msg.sender instead.
After a successful setOwner call by the current owner, the new owner must equal the address argument; the buggy version sets it to the caller, violating this for any caller different from _owner.
The return value of setOwner is always true in the reference, but false in the buggy version when called by the owner.

The owner can never change via setOwner; the buggy version makes this false when a non-owner caller succeeds in changing it (which they cannot in the reference), but the actual difference is that after a call to setOwner, the owner variable remains equal to the original owner in the reference, while in the buggy version the owner is never updated, so the invariant is that setOwner never alters the owner address.

After a successful call to setOwner with a new address by the current owner, the reference updates owner to that new address; the buggy version leaves owner unchanged, so the invariant 'owner equals the address passed to setOwner' holds for the reference but fails for the bug.
The setOwner function should succeed for the true owner, but the buggy onlyOwner modifier causes it to always revert, so the return value success is never true for any caller.
For any call to setOwner with a nonzero _owner, the contract's owner storage should update to that new address, but the buggy version always reverts so the owner never changes.
For any msg.sender when setOwner is called, the function should complete (not revert) and return true, but the buggy always-reverting modifier breaks this by causing every call to fail.
For any caller, a call to setOwner should either succeed (if the caller is owner) or revert; the buggy version always reverts, so the success flag is never true for any caller.
For any sender, a call to setOwner with any address argument should complete and modify owner only when the sender is the current owner; the buggy version always reverts regardless of sender.
For any caller that is not the owner, setOwner must revert; the buggy version allows any caller to change the owner.
